source: The app itself. Every question on the door tabs is a row of data/ledger-rows.json, in its own plain words; every figure on What it says is worked out by an engine in engines/, and the formula below is the same arithmetic written so a spreadsheet can do it.
confidenceNote: Nothing here is a new number, and nothing here is research: the tab names and the order are a convention, chosen so the file reads in the order worth filling it in. Each reading names the engine that owns it, and test/run.js fails if the sheet's formula and the engine disagree on any of the households it tries.
note: The workbook is one file: shared/workbook.js builds it, tools/workbook.js writes the blank one, rooms/data.html hands you yours. D-356.
title: Money Rooms

doors.blurb: Who the household is. Everything else leans on these.
What comes in, and whether it would keep coming.
What a month costs. The single most useful number in the file.
Cash, investments, and anything else worth something.
One line per debt: the balance, the rate, the smallest payment.
Only what the other tabs need. This is not a tax return.

assumptions.name: swrRate
assumptions.label: The share of a pot you could draw a year
assumptions.words: The 4% convention. It is a rule of thumb, not a law; change it here and the FI number below changes with it.

readings.label: Pay, a year, before tax
readings.words: Every line on Money in, added up.

readings.label: Pay, a month, before tax
readings.words: A year of pay divided by twelve.

readings.label: Everything you own
readings.words: Cash and investments, plus anything else on What you own.

readings.label: What a month really costs
readings.words: The month, plus a twelfth of the once-a-year bills, because they arrive whether the month is ready or not.

readings.label: If the pay stopped, months you could go
readings.words: Cash divided by a month. The one number worth knowing before any other.

readings.label: The cushion you are aiming at
readings.words: Three months of spending, or six when the pay swings.

readings.label: How much of that cushion you have
readings.words: Cash against the cushion. Over 100% means it is built.

readings.label: Share of pay you keep
readings.words: What you put away each month against what you earn before tax.

readings.label: Share of take-home you spend
readings.words: The month against what actually lands in the account.

readings.label: Share of take-home the roof takes
readings.words: Rent or mortgage against take-home. Much over a third and everything else gets tight.

readings.label: Share of take-home the minimums take
readings.words: What you must pay on debts each month, against take-home.

readings.label: Debt to income, the lender's way
readings.words: The roof plus the minimums, against pay before tax. A mortgage lender reads this one.

readings.label: What the debt costs you a month
readings.words: Interest alone, before a penny comes off any balance.

readings.label: The rate you are really paying
readings.words: Every rate, weighted by how much sits at it.

readings.label: What you owe against what you own
readings.words: Under 100% means you own more than you owe.

readings.label: Share of what you own you could reach
readings.words: Cash and investments against everything, including the things you would have to sell.

readings.label: Net worth against a year of pay
readings.words: How many years of pay you have already banked.

readings.label: If you stopped today, what you would draw
readings.words: A year of spending against the pot. Beside the 4% below, this says how far off the day is.

readings.label: The pot that would cover the month forever
readings.words: A year of spending divided by the draw rate above. The convention, not a promise.
